title: Does a perfect cuboid exist?
credit: Classical (Euler; Kraitchik; listed as D18 in Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory).
premise_risks: Several unrefereed 2026 nonexistence claims (arXiv:2602.00239 math.GM, arXiv:2604.28072) exist; none accepted, but the scorer should know they are out there
plain: Is there a box whose three edges, three face diagonals and space diagonal all have whole-number lengths? Boxes with whole-number edges and face diagonals (Euler bricks, such as 44 × 117 × 240) come in infinite families, but in every known one the space diagonal is irrational. Nobody has found a perfect box or proved that none exists.
math: Decide whether there exist positive integers $a,b,c$ such that $a^2+b^2$, $b^2+c^2$, $c^2+a^2$ and $a^2+b^2+c^2$ are all perfect squares.
